# CC13: 狮子林 Shizi Lin, "Lion Grove"

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC13` · Page: `/scenes/#CC13` · Row: `research/buildings/CC13-shizi-lin/`

## What it was

狮子林 Shizi Lin, "Lion Grove", in the north-east of Changchun Yuan, is two gardens: 丛芳榭 of 1747 on the lake (a five-bay hall with 琴清斋 behind it) and, to its east, the copy of the Suzhou 狮子林 finished in 1772 (E0223, E0165). Qianlong based it on 倪瓒's scroll and on the Suzhou garden, then owned by a 黄 family, with rockwork by Suzhou craftsmen (S05 j83:13b-15b; E0203). 日下旧闻考 lists its parts in order: 虹桥, 假山, 纳景堂, 清閟阁, 藤架, 磴道, 占峰亭, 清淑斋, 小香幢, 探真书屋, 延景楼, 云林石室, 横碧轩, 水门 (S05 j83:13b; E0220). He named eight scenes, then eight more, sixteen in all (E0219, E0218), and kept his copy of Ni Zan's painting in 清閟阁 (E0223). Jiaqing and Daoguang wrote on the sixteen scenes again; it was partly rebuilt in 1828, the dowager dined here in 1828-29 and the last entries are of 1858 (E0221, E0223). In 1856 the emperor gave seven officials a meal at 清淑斋 (E1524). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆三十七年 1772 [j83:13b]; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S48, S01, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not one of the Forty Scenes, but its own set: the 狮子林十六景 named by Qianlong in 1772-73, eight and then eight more (E0203, E0218, E0219), written again in 1775, 1779, 1781, 1786 and 1793, by Jiaqing in 1796 and Daoguang in 1828 (E0221). The Chengde copy (文园狮子林) bears the same names (E0219). He owns that the pines are young and that the Suzhou garden no longer matches Ni Zan's picture (E0218).

## What survives today

Ruin photographs of 2013 show the rainbow bridge and the water gate restored on their sites and the ruins of the east part (P0415, P0416, P0500, P0443). No dig report found in this round's searches.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.

## Gaps and wishlist

Only two of the 14 named parts have a plan size (清閟阁 7 bays, 探真书屋); the rockery's form rests on the Suzhou garden and the Chengde copy, which are comparables, not evidence. No Yangshi Lei plan of the compound is in the catalogue.

### Open questions that name it

- **Q119. Digs.** Digs: by the park's own list (S946, 2024) and what this round found, no excavation has been published for YM03 九洲清晏 (survey only, S151), YM02 勤政亲贤, YM29 方壶胜境, YM32 蓬岛瑶台, YM44 同乐园, YM15 山高水长 (1994 auger survey only, S156), YM38, YM33, CC13 狮子林, CC04 思永斋, YM17 安佑宫 or QC01. Sizes there must come from Yangs
- **Q214. The age of the pines.** Qianlong's preface of 1770 says Changchun Yuan's pines were planted as saplings (S05 j83 "培松拱把"; at 狮子林 "稚松皆新種"); by 1860 they were about 90 years old. 清晖阁's pines burned in 1763 and were replanted (S361). All pines are drawn as mature trees of 12 m, a species default. (Round 12)
